_howTo.readMe: This file holds ALL the clinic details for the website and the app. Full guide: README.md (section 4). This _howTo section is ignored by the website, so it is safe to leave here.
_howTo.editingRules: Only change text INSIDE the quotes "...". Keep quotes, colons and commas. true/false have no quotes. When adding a list item, copy an existing { ... } item and put a comma between items but not after the last one. Check the file at jsonlint.com before publishing. If the file has a mistake, the build stops and the live site stays as it was.
_howTo.settings: showInstallButton: false for now; true shows an "Install the app" button (app phase). themeColor = colour of the phone top bar in the app.
_howTo.logo: The logo mark (cross and paw) is saved in the site at src/assets/icons/logo-mark.png and set in logo.url as "/assets/icons/logo-mark.png". The app icons and browser-tab icon are in src/assets/icons (made from the PawMedics square logo). To use a different logo instead, either put a file in src/assets/brand and give its path starting with /, or upload it to imgbb.com, open it, choose "Direct links" and paste the link that starts with https://i.ibb.co/ (ending .png or .jpg) into logo.url. The normal https://ibb.co/ page link will NOT work. For the phone app icon, upload a SQUARE 512 x 512 PNG and paste its direct link into logo.appIconUrl. Set showNameNextToLogo to false if the logo already contains the name. alt = description for screen readers. Leave fields empty ("") to keep the placeholder paw. The build saves a copy of the images inside the site; if it cannot download them (wrong link, or built somewhere without internet access, e.g. by Claude), it still finishes and links to ImgBB directly instead (works, but not offline).
_howTo.clinic: address: line1 = number and street, then locality, postcode and country (postcode is shown in the full address and given to Google). phone = how the number is shown; phoneInternational = what phones dial (keep +356).
_howTo.links: EVERY link and button on the site, grouped by page (everyPage = top bar, menu, footer and the phone's bottom Call/Book bar). Each has its own text and url, so each booking button can go to a different place: change one and the others stay as they are. A url can be a full web address (https://...) or a page on this site (/acupuncture/, /#contact). Entries with text but no url are Call or Email buttons: they always use the phone number or email in clinic, and the number or email is shown with the text automatically (the narrow Call button in the phone's bottom bar shows the text only). topBarAddress is the address shown in the top bar (kept short so the bar fits on one line); the full address comes from clinic.address. Its url is also given to Google as the clinic's map. The other clinic is linked from three places, each set separately: topBarSisterClinic (top bar on every page; hidden on phones to save space), heroSisterClinic (the line under the main booking buttons on the home page) and homePage.sisterClinic (the Vetcare card in "Two clinics, one team"). footerFacebook's url is also given to Google as the clinic's Facebook page. The menu is a list: copy an item to add a menu link. app = the shortcuts shown when the installed app's icon is long-pressed on Android; the acupuncture shortcut must be a page on this site. Two links are fixed on purpose: the logo always goes to the home page, and the hidden "Skip to content" link for screen readers.
_howTo.hours: 24-hour times, e.g. "19:00" (shown as 7pm). For a closed day use "closed": true. schemaDays = English day names the row covers (used by Google). Hours appear in the top bar, contact section, footer and offline page.
_howTo.notices: Messages shown in a bar at the very top of every page, for example Christmas hours or a closure. Each notice appears by itself on its "from" date and disappears by itself after its "until" date (Malta time), so notices can be added weeks ahead and need no extra publish to switch on or off. Dates are written year-month-day, e.g. "2026-12-24". "show": false switches a notice off completely. linkText and linkUrl are optional (both or neither). Several notices can be listed; all that are in date show. Copy an existing { ... } item to add one.
_howTo.emergency: The same message also appears in the first FAQ and in the "Summer heat" tip; update those too if it changes.
_howTo.vets: Keep Dr. Andrew FIRST and Dr. Teresa SECOND: the home-page photo pair with the "Vet / Not Vets" arrows and the acupuncture page depend on this order. Further vets (e.g. Dr. Adam) go after them and appear in "Meet our vets". "partner": true marks the clinic partners (named in "Two clinics, one team"). Bios starting "[Placeholder bio]" are dummy text to replace; an empty bio is hidden. photo = image name in src/assets/img. If Dr. Andrew's or Dr. Teresa's photo is replaced, ask Claude to redraw the arrows.
_howTo.bookOnline: The "What you can book online" cards on the home page. Each card has its own button text and link (linkText, linkUrl), so if Provet gives a direct link for a booking type it can go here. notSure is the line under the cards; the phone number and email are added automatically. "show": false hides the section.
_howTo.about: The "About PawMedics" section on the home page: paragraphs (one per item), a photo with its caption. "show": false hides it.
_howTo.gallery: The "Care in action" photo strip on the home page. Each item = photo name in src/assets/img, alt (description for screen readers) and caption. Add, remove or reorder freely; "show": false hides it.
_howTo.reviews: "show": false on a single review hides just that card (Keith C. is kept that way so a 3-across layout stays even). The Google rating and the review cards on the home page. rating and count are typed in by hand, so update them now and then from Google (they also show under the main booking buttons). Each item is one review card: name (first name and initial), stars (1 to 5) and text. Keep the reviewer's own words; where a review is shortened, mark the missing part with … . Add, remove or reorder items freely; set "show": false to hide the whole section. The links to Google are links.homePage.heroReviews and links.homePage.reviewsAll.
_howTo.services: "show": true/false shows or hides a service (set false for anything the Swatar clinic does not offer). "featured": true = purple outline. "link" adds a link at the bottom of the card; "linkText" is its wording ("Learn more" if left out).
_howTo.maltaTips: icon can be bug, sun, plane or paw.
_howTo.faq: Home-page questions; the first one is shown open.
_howTo.acupuncture: photo = picture in the home-page acupuncture block; pagePhoto = picture at the top of the acupuncture page; gallery = the dogs / cats / rabbits photos on the acupuncture page. homeTeaser = text in the home-page acupuncture block. fees is empty, so no fees box shows. Add rows like { "label": "Initial consultation", "price": "€XX" } and the fees box appears automatically with a Book button (its wording and link are links.acupuncturePage.feesBook).

about.title: About PawMedics
paragraphs: PawMedics offers compassionate veterinary care for small animals from our practice in Swatar. Since opening in 2025 we have looked after dogs, cats, rabbits and other small pets, with consultations, vaccinations, acupuncture, at-home euthanasia and more.
In 2026 Vetcare Animal Clinic in San Ġwann joined us. Vetcare clients still see the same trusted team and familiar faces, with continued improvements ahead.
We also love being part of the community, from school careers days to helping young future vets meet their first patients.

maltaTips.title: Sandflies & leishmaniasis
maltaTips.text: Sandflies spread leishmaniasis to dogs in Malta. Ask us about repellent collars, vaccination and yearly screening before the warm months.

maltaTips.title: Summer heat
maltaTips.text: Walk early or late, check pavements with your hand and never leave a pet in a car. Heavy panting or collapse is an emergency: call us straight away, or the government emergency vet clinic in Fgura if we're closed.

maltaTips.title: Travelling or relocating
maltaTips.text: Moving to or from Malta? We handle microchips, rabies vaccination, EU pet passports and health certificates. Book early, as some steps need weeks.

maltaTips.title: New puppy or kitten?
maltaTips.text: Your first visit covers a health check, a vaccination plan, microchipping and worming, plus time for all your questions.

faq.q: What should I do in an emergency?
faq.a: We don't run an out-of-hours service. During opening hours, call 2133 5793 and come straight in. When we're closed, please go to the government's National Veterinary Emergency Service clinic in Reggie Miller Square, Fgura.

faq.q: How do I book an appointment?
faq.a: Book online at any time through our booking page, or call us during opening hours.

faq.q: Is acupuncture safe for my pet?
faq.a: Dr. Teresa starts with a full examination to check acupuncture suits your pet. Most animals relax during sessions, and it can be combined with their usual medication.

faq.q: Can you come to my home?
faq.a: We offer at-home euthanasia so your pet can say goodbye peacefully at home. Please call us to arrange it.

acupuncture.homeTeaser: Dr. Teresa practises Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) acupuncture. It is a gentle, drug-free treatment used alongside conventional care, and is often chosen for older pets and long-term conditions.
whatIsIt: Very fine, sterile needles are placed at specific points on the body to help relieve pain and support healing. Dr. Teresa uses Traditional Chinese Veterinary Medicine (TCVM) alongside modern veterinary medicine. It works with your pet's usual treatment and does not replace it.
Most pets become calm, and many fall asleep during a session.
helpsWith: Arthritis and joint stiffness in older pets

steps.title: Initial consultation
steps.text: A full examination and review of your pet's history, to check acupuncture is suitable.

steps.title: A tailored plan
steps.text: Dr. Teresa explains the plan and how many sessions she expects your pet to need.

steps.title: Calm sessions
steps.text: Sessions take place in a quiet room, and you can stay with your pet.

steps.title: Review progress
steps.text: We track how your pet is moving and feeling, and adjust the plan as needed.

faq.a: The needles are much finer than injection needles. Most pets barely notice them and relax within a few minutes.

faq.q: How many sessions will my pet need?
faq.a: It depends on the condition. Dr. Teresa will give you an expected plan at the first consultation.
